text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in Norwegian papers this morning:
- Norway's Central Bank upgraded its forecast for 1997 Gross Domestic Product growth by 0.5 percentage points to 3.5 percent and said Norway was facing a prolonged upturn now into its fourth year.
- Prime Minister Torbjoern Jagland threatened to resign if the opposition continues to hound his justice minister over a scandal involving the national intelligence service.
- The general assembly in telecommunications group Nera ASA unanimously agreed to increase the company's captial and to list Nera on the Singapore bourse.
- Kvaerner ASA has entered an agreement with Thyssen Rheinstahl Technik GmbH, Kloeckner Industrie-Anlagen GmbH and Altmark-Industrie AG to form a company to build the world's largest pulp plant.

- Norwegian shipping company Leih Hoegh & Co. ASA, Britain's Tufton Oceanic and South-African Safmarine are forming the worlds largests operating company for refrigerated carrier ships. The new company will be called UniCool Ltd and will be registrered in Bermuda.
